narrative.overview:
A settled middle position arrived at across three builds: a metaphor-led design was rejected as a gimmick, and the plain neutral rebuild that replaced it was rejected as bland and incoherent. The structure is ordinary and sections are named for what they hold; there is no governing metaphor. But the page is not neutral-by-default either — it carries a voice through warm paper, a text serif, small-caps metadata, a specific warm accent, and numbered sections.

The ground is a functional decision. Two of the three featured products are dark-UI; against stark white their screenshots read as pasted on, and against warm paper with a band-toned mat they sit in the page. That single change is most of what separates this from the version that felt incoherent.
keyCharacteristics: No metaphor, but not voiceless either
Warm paper ground chosen to serve dark-UI screenshots
One deep-rust accent, deliberately not terracotta
Serif for sentences, condensed small-caps for furniture
Limitations get their own labelled block
Flat and square — no shadow, no radius
Printerly detail — grain, masthead rule, numbered figures, a drop cap

rules.name: The Rust, Not Terracotta Rule
rules.body: The obvious accent for warm paper is terracotta, and it is both the default this palette must avoid and an accessibility failure: #c1553a measures 4.10:1 on this ground, under the floor. The accent is deliberately deeper and browner. Do not lighten it.

rules.name: The Both Grounds Rule
rules.body: Every text value is measured against the ground it actually sits on — paper, band, or the dark equivalents — and both schemes are audited every pass. No theme toggle; the OS already knows.

rules.name: The Furniture Rule
rules.body: Archivo Narrow only labels; it never sets a sentence. If a line has a subject and a verb it is Petrona.

rules.name: The Numeral Rule
rules.body: Major sections carry a Roman numeral in accent small-caps. These are information: each page states an order. Never number a page with a single section.

rules.name: The Real Screenshot Rule
rules.body: Every product image is captured from the live application after it has been driven into a real working state. Empty states, mockups and illustrations standing in for the product are not permitted.

rules.name: The Limitation Is Not A Footnote Rule
rules.body: A limitation gets its own labelled block near the claim it qualifies, never a parenthetical at the end. This is the one place the accent appears on a non-interactive element, and it is earned.

rules.name: No Metaphor
rules.body: Standing constraint recorded in PRODUCT.md. No conceit, no borrowed vocabulary, no conceptual layer over the content — and none smuggled back as a detail.

rules.name: The Printing Family Rule
rules.body: Detail beyond the strictly necessary — grain, masthead rule, figure numbers, drop cap — is drawn only from the conventions of a well-set printed document. The subject is a published researcher and the site argues for careful evidence, so the ornament is the kind a journal or proof sheet would have. Nothing decorative enters from outside that family.

rules.name: The Figure Rule
rules.body: Every screenshot and diagram is a numbered figure with a hairline, Fig. n in accent small-caps, and a description. Numbering is not ornament: it is how a reader refers to an image, and it commits the page to saying what each one shows. An image that cannot earn a caption should not be on the page.

rules.name: The Legibility Rule
rules.body: A screenshot is evidence, so its own text must be readable. A capture wider than the reading column breaks out to the wide column rather than being downscaled into it, and a panel is clipped to the part that carries the argument rather than shown whole. A screenshot whose text cannot be read has become decoration.

rules.name: The One Screen Rule
rules.body: On an index page a project card must fit a laptop screen together with its detail — title, description, tags, links. That caps the screenshot near 355px tall on desktop (aspect-[8/3], top-cropped; aspect-[16/10] below sm, where a sliver would show nothing). Verified at 1280x800 and 1440x900.

rules.name: The Capture, Not The Crop Rule
rules.body: When a top-crop would waste the frame on a sparse header, re-capture the source clipped to the region that carries the argument rather than fudging it with object-position.

rules.name: The Crop Only Downward Rule
rules.body: A card frame crops an image only when the image is taller than the frame. A capture already wider than the frame is shown whole: object-cover on a too-wide source scales it up to fill the height and cuts the sides off, which reads as a zoom and hides content.

dos: Capture screenshots from the live product, in a real working state, and mat them.
Measure contrast against the actual ground, in both schemes.
Give a limitation its own labelled block near the claim it qualifies.
Set furniture in Archivo Narrow and sentences in Petrona, always.
Keep prose at 66ch and supporting text in muted.
Use tabular numerals wherever figures are read down a column.
Clip a screenshot to the panel that carries the argument, and let it break out of the reading column so its text stays legible.
Verify a card fits a laptop viewport with its detail, by measuring, not by eye.
donts: Don't introduce a metaphor, theme, or conceptual frame.
Don't drift the accent toward terracotta — it is the default here and it fails contrast.
Don't warm the paper into cream or ivory.
Don't add shadows, and don't round anything.
Don't set prose or navigation in the condensed face.
Don't number a page that has no sequence.
Don't ship a mockup or empty-state capture where a real screenshot belongs.
Don't add ornament from outside the printing family — no gradients, glows, or illustrative flourishes.
Don't use box-shadow even to draw a line; borders and pseudo-elements do that job.
